clue.text: Aromatic vein of ore turning up in fissure

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, so these words place the vein within the crack

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a lode is a vein of metal ore in rock

explanation.surface: A miner smells something fragrant drifting from a vein of ore in a crack in the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent describes something giving off a strong pleasant smell, a straightforward synonym for fragrant.

clue.text: Assembly dismissing University document

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so one letter is sent out of the assembly word

parts.note: a forum is a public meeting or assembly
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A gathering sends a university's paperwork packing.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a printed sheet with spaces to fill in, which is a kind of official paper.

clue.text: Bank upset about court orders

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word wraps round the abbreviation
in a down entry, something upset is turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a river's side is its bank
CT is the usual abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A bank in turmoil faces rulings from a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court orders' reads as one phrase, but court supplies only its abbreviation and orders alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official decrees or commands issued by an authority, so they are orders in that formal sense.

clue.text: Fellow on farm given a scarf

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to till is to plough and work the land
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmhand is handed a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is the charade signal that one piece comes after another; farm here is a verb, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace or silk scarf worn over the head and shoulders, especially by Spanish women.

clue.text: Monitor about to resort to drink

parts.note: to chart is to record and track, i.e. to monitor
re means about or concerning
to resort to something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone keeping watch is about to turn to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the verge of', but about gives its own letters and to only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, so it is one particular alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Intense part of standard entertainment

indicators.note: part of tells you the letters form only a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something intense forms part of ordinary entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and fervent, feeling something with great strength, so it matches intense.

clue.text: Stenographer's instrument

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who takes down a spoken record
second meaning: a simple woodwind pipe played in schools

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like the shorthand writer owns one tool; the two words are separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who writes down proceedings keeps a record, and the same word names the wooden end-blown flute.

clue.text: Retired queen has surprising tale to tell

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the royal abbreviation goes backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the queen

indicators.note: surprising suggests something unexpected, so the letters turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A former monarch has an astonishing story to share.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or recount it, which is to tell it.

clue.text: A runaway horse is on the beach

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a runaway is out of control, so the letters break loose from their order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An escaped horse is galloping along the sands.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land beside the sea, so it describes being on the coast rather than in the water.

clue.text: John has master's weaving equipment

parts.note: john and loo are both slang for a toilet
M is an abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: A man called John owns his master's weaving gear.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a name but is American slang for a toilet; loo is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A loom is the frame on which threads are interlaced to make cloth.

clue.text: Unsympathetic country offering unpleasant cure for addiction

parts.note: cold means unfeeling or unsympathetic
Turkey is a country

explanation.surface: A harsh nation provides a grim treatment for drug addicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Going cold turkey means stopping an addictive drug abruptly, an idiom for a harsh withdrawal treatment.

clue.text: Mediterranean island the French cry about

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a cry is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: The French complain about a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesbos is a large Greek island in the northeastern Aegean, part of the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Flaps of skin wobbling in big gowns?

indicators.note: wobbling means shaking unsteadily, so the letters shift about into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these three words is used, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Loose flesh jiggles inside large dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: Bingo wings is British slang for the loose skin under the upper arms that wobbles when waving, as at a bingo hall; the whole clue also describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo wings are the sagging folds hanging from the upper arm, a colloquial name for flabby underarm flesh.

clue.text: Large kind of bag containing real dancing bear

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the bag wraps around the rearranged word

parts.note: a tote is a large carrier bag

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the next word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A big bag holds a genuine dancing bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing bear' is a stock phrase, but bear here is a verb and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with or endure it, the verb sense matching tolerate.

clue.text: One renting basic accommodation outside centre of Monaco

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the shelter goes round the selected letters

parts.note: a tent is the simplest kind of shelter

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are taken

parts.note: the two middle letters of the six-letter name

explanation.surface: A renter makes do with a simple pad on the edge of Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person who occupies property in return for paying rent to its owner.

clue.text: Letter by grand American conservative is worthless

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
G is short for grand, slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
A is the abbreviation for American
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A note from a wealthy American right-winger is of no value.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or importance, or having no force, a formal synonym for worthless.

clue.text: Bad painting taking in north European river

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing within, so the painting word holds the compass letter

parts.note: a daub is a crude, badly executed painting
N is the abbreviation for north
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A poor picture depicts a river in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North European river' reads as one phrase; north and European each give a single letter and river alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danube is a major river flowing from Germany through central Europe to the Black Sea.

clue.text: Unconventional nineties genius

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order or form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: every letter is used, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An offbeat thinker from the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the physicist of relativity, is so famous for brilliance that his name stands for any genius.

clue.text: English fighting over Germany to get daughter to an old king

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
war is armed fighting, here placed after the code for Germany
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: England goes to war against Germany for the sake of a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run English, Germany, fighting, daughter, so 'over' cannot mean placed on top here; read it loosely as war being waged beyond Germany. Edward was the name of eight English kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English monarchs bore this name, from Edward the Confessor onward, so it identifies a former ruler.

clue.text: Swollen bananas go green — close to bad

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: every letter is used, then rearranged

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Bloated bananas turn green and are nearly rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas looks like the fruit being described, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Engorged means swollen or filled to excess, typically with blood or fluid.

clue.text: Enthusiast served up perfect example of spice

parts.note: a nut is a keen fan, as in a fitness nut

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means sent upwards, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a gem is a perfect or outstanding example

explanation.surface: A keen cook offers up a fine example of a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a common kitchen spice.

clue.text: Sponges found by climber heading to slopes

indicators.note: a heading is at the top, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
to lean is to slope or tilt

explanation.surface: Sea sponges are discovered by a mountaineer on the way to the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sponges looks like a noun for sea creatures, but it is a verb meaning wipes clean; 'to' hitches onto slopes rather than heading.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge something is to wipe or wash it with a damp sponge, so sponges is a synonym for washes.

clue.text: Tuck sides of robe into luggage

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the kept letters go within the luggage word

parts.note: a case is a suitcase

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outer edges, so its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Fold the edges of a dressing gown into a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck is a flattened fold sewn or pressed into fabric, which is a crease in cloth.

clue.text: Entertainment offered by naughty priest carrying drinks?

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the rearranged word holds the drinks
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters fail to stay in order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
cups of tea are drinks

explanation.surface: A wayward clergyman puts on a show while serving refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cheeky idea of a naughty priest providing this sort of show.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a performance in which someone undresses slowly to music, a form of adult show.

clue.text: Try to back clubs

indicators.note: to back means to go backwards, so the word for an attempt is written in the other direction

parts.note: to have a stab is to have a try

explanation.surface: An attempt to support a set of golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like support, as in backing a team, but here it means reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats used in cricket or baseball are wooden striking implements, just like clubs.

clue.text: Raised money for speakers

indicators.note: for speakers means as heard by those talking, so the word counts by sound not spelling

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Funds were collected to pay for loudspeakers.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised money looks like fundraising, but raised alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred is the past tense of breed, meaning brought up or reared, as children or livestock are.

clue.text: Account book found by shelf on right

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A book of accounts is discovered on a shelf to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is the charade signal that one piece follows another.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger is the principal book in which a business records its financial transactions.

clue.text: Daily sex sorted out learning difficulty

indicators.note: sorted out means rearranged or put in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: every letter of both words is used, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Having sex every day has fixed someone's problem with reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyslexia is a condition affecting reading and spelling despite normal intelligence, a recognised specific learning disability.
